summary: The main article describes a dual phosphine and photoredox catalytic system for the anti-Markovnikov hydroamination of olefins. It includes 1 table for reaction optimization, 5 figures detailing mechanistic proposals, quenching studies, and substrate scopes for both olefins and sulfonamides.

items.heading: Figure 1
items.caption: Synthesis and reactivity of phosphoranyl radicals.
items.description: Illustrates the general pathways for phosphoranyl radical fragmentation (alpha vs beta scission) and the proposed catalytic hydroamination strategy.

items.heading: Figure 2
items.caption: Proposed catalytic cycle and alternative speciation pathways.
items.description: Detailed catalytic cycle showing the role of phosphine and photoredox catalysts, along with potential side reactions and decomposition pathways.

items.heading: Table 1
items.caption: Optimization studies
items.description: Screening of phosphine ligands, photocatalysts, bases, and stoichiometry for the hydroamination of 1-hexene with p-tert-butylbenzenesulfonamide.

items.heading: Figure 3A
items.caption: Alternative mechanism: N-H activation via proton-coupled electron transfer
items.description: Depicts a potential PCET pathway for N-H bond activation as an alternative to the phosphoranyl radical mechanism.

items.heading: Figure 3B
items.caption: Alternative mechanism: C-N bond formation from P(V) intermediate
items.description: Shows a possible reductive elimination pathway from a pentavalent phosphorus intermediate.

items.heading: Figure 3D
items.caption: Catalytic performance of isolated P-derived byproducts
items.description: Experimental results testing the catalytic activity of isolated phosphorus byproducts like imidophosphoranes and aminophosphines.

items.heading: Figure 3E
items.caption: Evaluation of P(V) mechanism with mixed n-alkyl ligands
items.description: Mechanistic experiment using triethylphosphine to distinguish between radical scission and reductive elimination pathways.

items.heading: Figure 4
items.caption: Olefin scope.
items.description: Displays the variety of acyclic, cyclic, and functionalized olefins that are compatible with the hydroamination conditions.

items.heading: Figure 5
items.caption: Sulfonamide scope.
items.description: Shows the scope of primary aryl and alkyl sulfonamides, including medicinally relevant structures, used in the reaction.
